name: 自然食カフェ シマカラ食堂 (Shizenshoku Cafe Shimakara Shokudo)

claims.text: The kitchen uses traditional island-made soy sauce in many dishes; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so non-GF-labeled dishes should be assumed to contain wheat.

No specific cross-contamination protocols or allergen warnings are published; the cafe was founded partly to serve people with allergy concerns, and customers with allergies are advised to contact the restaurant directly at 082-236-9303.
Specific menu items are explicitly labeled gluten-free, including a vegan potato croquette set and a soy-meat fried 'chicken' dish.
All seasonings are additive-free, rice is pesticide-free, oil is non-GMO cold-pressed rapeseed, and chicken is free-range and antibiotic-free.
Clearly identified plant-based options (vegan croquette, soy meat, tofu sets) make it straightforward for vegans to order safely.

name: Yamaichi Bekkan (割烹旅館 山一別館)

claims.text: Shared ryokan kitchen, not a dedicated GF facility; GF is achieved by remaking dishes on request. Confirm cross-contact precautions when phoning ahead.
Standard kaiseki uses wheat-based soy sauce; the venue says dishes can be changed to gluten-free 「可能な限り、全てのお料理をグルテンフリー仕様に変更できます」 — confirm tamari/wheat-free seasoning is used for your meal.
Dedicated plant-based kaiseki course prepared to be animal-free including seasonings; still a shared kitchen, so arrange in advance.
The venue explicitly requests advance phone contact to arrange allergy/GF meals: 「事前にお電話にて詳細をお知らせくださいませ」 (TEL 0829-44-0700).
One of the only GF-accommodating dining spots on Miyajima island itself; willing to convert full courses to gluten-free with notice.

name: 野菜to発芽酵素玄米弁当 YOU&I (Yasai to Hatsuga Koso Genmai Bento YOU&I (TA)

claims.text: The shop states that wheat is completely avoided even in seasonings such as soy sauce, and no wheat flour or gluten-containing ingredients are used in any item.
Entirely dedicated gluten-free kitchen: all menu items are gluten-free, with rice flour replacing breadcrumbs in fried dishes and wheat excluded even from seasonings.
A genuinely vegan bento with no animal-derived ingredients, based on traditional Japanese shojin (Buddhist) cuisine, is offered daily (limited to 10).
COIL is a shared sushi and tempura kitchen handling wheat-based items; no dedicated gluten-free prep area or fryer is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is likely despite the gluten-free course.
No wheat-free tamari is documented; standard Japanese soy sauce used with sushi typically contains wheat, so the soy sauce here should be assumed to contain wheat unless staff confirm otherwise.
Vegan/精進 ingredients are assembled in the same venue that serves fish, seafood, roast beef and cheese; shared rice, surfaces and utensils mean cross-contact with animal products is possible.
Staff actively created and demonstrate vegan/精進 and gluten-free sets for guests with diverse dietary needs, but no formal allergen protocol is published.
Offers clearly labeled dedicated vegan/精進 and gluten-free hand-roll courses, bookable in advance, which is unusual for a Kanazawa sushi venue.
The vegan soy-milk mayonnaise is explicitly made without dairy or eggs.
All sweets are brown-/white-rice-flour based and stated 「小麦粉不使用」, but no certified dedicated-kitchen claim was found.
Not applicable — dessert/bakery shop.
Muffins are vegan; chiffon may contain egg — made in the same kitchen.
Positions products as additive-free and wheat/dairy-free; check Instagram for allergen details per batch.
Tea flavour confirmed as 加賀棒茶 roasted green stem tea, not barley tea (麦茶) — no barley gluten risk.

name: Conconto Kashiten (コンコント菓子店)

claims.text: 全商品、卵や乳製品、小麦粉、そば、落花生など食物アレルギー物質の特定原材料7品目は使わず、米や豆など植物性の食材のみでつくる — no wheat, soba or peanut is present anywhere in production, so cross-contact risk is minimal.
Dessert-only patisserie; no soy sauce used in the sweets menu.
Entirely plant-based kitchen — dairy replaced by soy-milk ice cream and custard, no eggs used, so vegan cross-contact is not a concern.
Shop is explicitly built around allergy safety, making items suitable for people with allergies as well as those without.
100% wheat-free, buckwheat-free and peanut-free dedicated plant-based patisserie with sit-in cafe — a standout safe option in Kanazawa.

name: Komeko Chiffon Kokone (米粉シフォン 心寧)

claims.text: 「調理場含め、作業場等に小麦粉は一切置いていないので小麦アレルギーの方も安心してお召し上がり頂けます。」 — no wheat flour is kept anywhere on the premises, kitchen included, so wheat-allergic guests can eat safely.
「小麦粉を使わず国産米粉100％で丁寧に作る、米粉シフォンケーキ専門店」 — a rice-flour-only chiffon specialty shop that uses no wheat flour; corroborates a wheat-free operation. Self-declared, no certification/ppm testing published.
Not applicable — sweets-and-coffee-only shop with no savory dishes, so no soy sauce or miso is used in any product.
All items contain egg; cheese and cup-chiffon items contain dairy. No vegan/egg-free preparation exists, so vegan cross-contact is moot.

Run by the two sister-owners themselves (a former nurse and a former childcare worker); the whole business is built around allergen-conscious food, but no formal documented allergen-handling protocol was found beyond the no-wheat-on-premises statement.
Dedicated rice-flour-only shop: 100% domestic 米粉, no wheat kept on premises, additive/coloring/preservative-free, and no wheat baked on-site.
Sweets-only menu removes the soy-sauce/miso wheat trap entirely.
General cafe with heavy wheat use — 4 wheat pastas, hot sandwiches, bread and a chili dog — sharing the same kitchen as the rice waffle; no dedicated GF prep area or utensil separation is published.
No allergen or cross-contact statement appears in any source; the '完全グルテンフリー' label describes the waffle recipe only.
Hayashi rice roux conventionally contains wheat flour — treat as NOT gluten-free despite being served over rice. Onigiri/miso-set seasonings and dashi are unverified for wheat.
Not vegan; butter, honey and dairy used across sweets. Any plant-based onigiri share a kitchen with meat fillings and wheat items.
No published allergy-handling policy; verify by phone (076-259-1100).
Flagship waffle uses 白山市産米粉100% and is marketed as 「米粉を100%使用した完全グルテンフリースイーツ」.
Hakusan City government confirms the sweets use 100% Hakusan-grown rice flour (chisan-chisho certified).
